title: Projection formula for extension by zero along a locally closed immersion
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $X$ a standing scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and
$a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ a locally closed immersion, with
$u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ open and $i\colon\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ closed, and
$a_!=i_*u_!$. For $M\in\D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and $L\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
there is a natural isomorphism
$$
(a_!M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}L\simeq a_!\bigl(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_S}a^*L\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda).
$$
Here $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], $\D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ is the unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and the tensor is the relative K-flat derived tensor [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules]. The functors $u_!$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], $i_*$ [def-sfb-module-lower-star], and $a^*$ [def-sfb-module-upper-star] act termwise on complexes, using their exactness for these immersions.

proof.text: Work with actual module sheaves over the ring sheaf $B=\Lambda_Y$. A module object in abelian sheaves is precisely such a sheaf: evaluating its action gives $B(V)\times M(V)\to M(V)$ with the module axioms and semilinear restrictions; conversely the sectionwise bilinear actions induce $B\otimes M\to M$ through the sheafified tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The module-object equations become the sectionwise module equations in both directions. Morphisms coincide because their action square is exactly sectionwise linearity. A balanced bilinear map has the same universal property in both descriptions, and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] realizes it by sheafifying the sectionwise relative tensor; hence the identification preserves relative tensor. Thus it also identifies complexes and their quasi-isomorphisms. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], $f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_T$ for every immersion $f:T\to Y$, without restricting $\Lambda$ to finite or discrete coefficients. The pullback formula of [def-sfb-module-upper-star] therefore identifies $f^*$ with inverse image followed by transport across this ring isomorphism. The pushforward action of [def-sfb-module-lower-star] is the usual ringed direct-image action. For extension by zero, [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek] specifies the action $B\otimes j^{\Ab}_!M\cong j^{\Ab}_!(j^*B\otimes M)\to j^{\Ab}_!M$. On a section in the extension presheaf summand indexed by a factorization $V\to U$, this sends $b\otimes m$ to $b|_U m$; on the zero summand there is only the zero map. Sheafification gives exactly the ringed extension action. Restriction along the invertible $\alpha_j$ in [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] identifies its coefficients with $\Lambda_U$. Hence the ringed-site lemmas below apply to the specified module-object functors.

source.place: First paragraph: coefficient identification and exact module operations

proof.text: The standing schemes are separated and finite type over a field [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. A field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $(1)$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Its closed subscheme $\overline S$ is likewise finite type over the field: on the finitely many affine finite-type charts of $X$, take quotient coordinate rings. The same lemma makes $\overline S$ Noetherian. Every open subscheme of either is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], including after restriction to any affine chart. Thus $u$ and the open complements of each closed immersion used below are quasi-compact. These ambient schemes are qcqs: they are quasi-compact, and the intersection of two affine opens is an open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme and hence quasi-compact by the same open-subscheme lemma. This verifies the quasi-compact-complement and qcqs hypotheses needed below; no boundedness or constructibility is imposed on $M,L$.

source.place: First paragraph: hypotheses of open–closed localization

proof.text: For a complementary pair $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $i:T\hookrightarrow Y$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] supplies $j_!\dashv j^*$, the identities $j^*j_!=1$, $i^*i_*=1$, $i^*j_!=0$, $j^*i_*=0$, exactness of $j_!,i_*$, and $0\to j_!j^*N\to N\to i_*i^*N\to0$ for every $B$-module sheaf. Exactness of $j^*,i^*$ with the actual coefficient identifications is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. If both restrictions of a morphism are invertible, its kernel and cokernel have zero restrictions by exactness; their displayed localization sequences force them to be zero. Thus the two restrictions detect isomorphisms. This uses the ringed pro-etale sequence (Stacks Tags 09AA, 09BM, 09BN, 09AH), not geometric-stalk conservativity.

source.place: First paragraph: exactness, support identities, and joint detection

proof.text: Inverse image commutes with relative tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] (Stacks Tag 03EL). It also preserves coproducts: it is left adjoint to the module direct image [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], so apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. The same colimit lemma applies to $j_!\dashv j^*$ from step 3. Finally $i_*$ preserves small filtered colimits by the qcqs clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. It preserves finite direct sums since it is additive and exact. Writing $\bigoplus_{a\in A}N_a=\varinjlim_{F\subset A,\ F\text{ finite}}\bigoplus_{a\in F}N_a$ now shows that $i_*$ preserves all coproducts needed to totalize unbounded tensor complexes. The finite-subset index is a small filtered poset in the fixed module universe.

source.place: First and derived paragraphs: monoidal pullback and coproducts

proof.text: For sheaves $P$ on $V$ and $N$ on $Y$, form $\theta:j_!(P\otimes_{j^*B}j^*N)\to j_!P\otimes_B N$ as the $j_!\dashv j^*$ adjoint of $P\otimes j^*N\to j^*j_!P\otimes j^*N\cong j^*(j_!P\otimes N)$, using the unit and the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. Its $j^*$-restriction is the identity under $j^*j_!=1$, by the adjunction triangle identity. Its $i^*$-restriction has both source and target zero: use $i^*j_!=0$ and the same tensor comparison. The identities and joint detection in step 3, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and exact restriction, make $\theta$ an isomorphism. The construction is natural in both sheaves because the unit and tensor comparison are natural. Invert $\theta$ to obtain $j_!P\otimes_BN\cong j_!(P\otimes_{j^*B}j^*N)$.

For sheaves $P$ on $T$ and $N$ on $Y$, use the unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$ [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] to form $\psi:i_*P\otimes_BN\to i_*i^*(i_*P\otimes_BN)\cong i_*(P\otimes_{i^*B}i^*N)$. Here the last identification is the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] followed by the invertible closed counit. Under $i^*i_*=1$, the restriction $i^*\psi$ is the identity, by the triangle identity for this counit and unit. Both $j^*$-restrictions vanish since $j^*i_*=0$. The support identities and joint detection of step 3 again make $\psi$ an isomorphism. Every map used is natural in $P,N$.

Write $r=j^*$ and $e=j_!$, or $r=i^*$ and $e=i_*$. For arbitrary complexes $P,Q$, steps 5 and 6 give $eP^p\otimes_BQ^q\cong e(P^p\otimes_{rB}rQ^q)$, naturally in $p,q$. By the coproduct preservation proved in step 4 they sum over $p+q=n$ to an isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(eP\otimes_BQ)\cong e\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{rB}rQ)$. The total differential is $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]; naturality of the sheaf maps for $d_P$ and $d_Q$, and additivity of $e$, show that the isomorphism commutes with both summands and their signs. Likewise $r$ commutes with total tensor by step 4. Thus these are chain isomorphisms on unbounded complexes, not merely degreewise identifications. We also use the signed symmetry $P^p\otimes Q^q\to Q^q\otimes P^p$, $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$: the identities $(-1)^{(p+1)q}=(-1)^{pq+q}$ and $(-1)^{p(q+1)+p}=(-1)^{pq}$ check its two differential terms, and its square is the identity. This allows the K-flat tests below with either order of the factors.

source.place: Derived version: termwise maps and totalization

proof.text: If $Q$ is K-flat on $Y$ and $C$ is acyclic on the subscheme, then $eC$ is acyclic by exactness of $e$ (step 3). K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes $eC\otimes_BQ$ acyclic. Apply exact $r$ and use the totalized tensor comparison and $re=1$ to identify $r(eC\otimes_BQ)\cong C\otimes_{rB}rQ$. This proves $rQ$ K-flat. Moreover, if $Q^q$ is flat, apply the sheaf comparison to a short exact sequence $C'\to C\to C''$ on the subscheme: $e$ takes it to an exact sequence, tensoring with $Q^q$ preserves exactness, and applying exact $r$ identifies the result with tensoring the original sequence by $rQ^q$. Hence $rQ^q$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Derived version: inverse image preserves K-flatness

proof.text: For completeness $e$ also preserves flat-term K-flat complexes. If $P$ is K-flat and $C$ is acyclic on $Y$, exactness makes $rC$ acyclic. Step 7 identifies $eP\otimes_BC$ with $e(P\otimes_{rB}rC)$, which is acyclic: the signed symmetry of step 7 identifies $P\otimes rC$ with $rC\otimes P$, acyclic by K-flatness of $P$, and $e$ is exact. The same symmetry identifies $C\otimes eP$ with $eP\otimes C$. Thus $eP$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. If $P^p$ is flat, the sheaf formula identifies tensoring by $eP^p$ with the composite $e(P^p\otimes_{rB}r(-))$. Each of its three functors is exact, so $eP^p$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Derived version: flat-term models and resolution changes

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$ of $M,L$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], separately on the subscheme and ambient small ringed pro-etale sites. The exact termwise functors induce the specified derived functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Steps 8 and 9 show that $eP$ and $rQ$ are flat-term K-flat. The representative-computation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], applied separately over the two coefficient rings, identifies the two sides of step 7 with $eM\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L$ and $e(M\otimes_{rB}^{\mathbf L}rL)$. These are the relative derived tensors of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules] and [lem-sfb-derived-tensor-modules-derived]. Thus step 7 gives the desired isomorphism on representatives. The next two steps establish its naturality and independence of representatives.

source.place: Derived version: resolution computation and naturality

proof.text: The chain isomorphism of step 7 induces a natural isomorphism on the product of the two homotopy categories of flat-term K-flat complexes. Indeed, an additive termwise functor takes $f-g=dh+hd$ to the same equation. For total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], a homotopy in the first variable induces $h\otimes1$; in the second variable it induces $(-1)^p1\otimes h$ on a summand of first degree $p$. In each case expansion against $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ cancels the cross terms and leaves the required difference of tensor maps. Thus each bifunctor respects homotopies, and the naturality equation of step 7 passes to homotopy classes.

source.place: Derived version: resolution computation and naturality

proof.text: Put $A=rB$ on the subscheme. For $R=A,B$, let $\mathcal P_R$ be the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat complexes and $W_R$ its quasi-isomorphisms. The resolving-class equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes $q_R:\mathcal P_R\to D(R)$ a localization at $W_R$. Apply the product-localization clause of [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus] with $n=2$, $A_1=\mathcal P_A$, $A_2=\mathcal P_B$, and the full identity resolving subcategories explicitly permitted there. It says that $q_A\times q_B$ is a localization at $W_A\times W_B$. Step 10 identifies both bifunctors of step 11 with the restrictions of the desired derived bifunctors $U(M,L)=eM\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L$ and $V(M,L)=e(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}rL)$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to this product localization, with these representative comparisons as its $\phi_i$: the natural isomorphism of step 11 extends uniquely to a natural isomorphism $U\cong V$. This proves naturality in both derived variables and independence of representatives. The argument uses two different sites throughout; it does not apply the same-ring bifunctor clause of the tensor-descent node to mixed coefficients.

source.place: Tags 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization), 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization); natural-transformation universal property and product-localization supplied by the cited existing nodes

proof.text: Apply steps 10–12 first to the closed immersion $i$ with input $u_!M$ and $L$, and then to the open immersion $u$ with input $M$ and $i^*L$. This gives $i_*u_!M\otimes_{\Lambda_X}^{\mathbf L}L\cong i_*(u_!M\otimes_{\Lambda_{\overline S}}^{\mathbf L}i^*L)\cong i_*u_!(M\otimes_{\Lambda_S}^{\mathbf L}u^*i^*L)$. The composition identification $u^*i^*\cong a^*$ is [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]; exactness lets it act termwise. Substitute $a_!=i_*u_!$ to obtain exactly the displayed formula. Each isomorphism is natural in both variables by steps 10–12 and the natural composition identification.

proof_origin.place: First paragraph; Open immersions, sheaves; Closed immersions, sheaves; Derived version; Locally closed immersions. Details of totalization and resolving-class descent supplied explicitly.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q19-f25081881 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 13 steps against the cited statements and the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof (open/closed sheaf formulas, derived version, locally closed composition). The statement agrees with the blueprint; 'commutative' only makes explicit what the relative tensor and sk-def-sfb-dc-setting already require. The delivery adds no new nodes and no Mathlib leaves, and cites no SGA source. The repair splits former step 10 into three steps. Step 10 computes on representatives: lem-pc-kflat-resolution, the 'no resolution needed' clause of lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, and the representative clause of lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent applied separately to each ring, then identified with def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules through lem-sfb-derived-tensor-modules-derived. Step 11 is the elementary signed-homotopy check; the cross terms cancel. Step 12: each q_R is a localization by the descent node's equivalence clause, and lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus with n=2 and identity subcategories (explicitly permitted there) makes q_A x q_B a localization at W_A x W_B. Clause (2) of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property then extends the representative isomorphism uniquely to a natural isomorphism. The phi_i isomorphisms show that both bifunctors invert W; I also checked this directly through K-flat cones and the exactness of e. The same-ring clause is not misused on mixed coefficients. Steps 1-9 and 13 still check: the qcqs and quasi-compact-complement hypotheses for lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed, coproduct preservation for i_*, the totalization signs, preservation of K-flatness and flat terms in both directions, and u^*i^* = a^* through def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp. The route is fine: unit sk-lem-int-tensor uses sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom. I accept the generic tool uses in split_report. The duplicate search found only simplicial/Brown-specific localization nodes. Edge cases checked: empty S, identity immersions, the zero ring, unbounded complexes. No fixes.
